questions.question: Explain the Meaning of disabilities. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the Meaning of disabilities. -[U] / [CO2]- -1 marks
  • Disability refers to any physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory impairment that restricts a person’s ability to perform
  • normal daily activities. It results from the interaction between an individual’s condition and environmental barriers,
  • limiting participation in society.

questions.question: Categorize the mental disability and physical disability. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Categorize the mental disability and physical disability. - [An] / [CO2] -3 marks
  •  Mental Disability: Includes intellectual disability, mental illness, developmental disorders affecting thinking, behavior, and
  • learning.
  •  Physical Disability: Includes locomotor disability, visual and hearing impairments affecting body movement or senses.
  •  Basis of Classification: Mental relates to cognitive functioning; physical relates to bodily functions and mobility.

questions.question: Analyse professional challenges in rehabilitation practice. (Analyse – CO2). / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse professional challenges in rehabilitation practice. (Analyse – CO2). - An] / [CO6]
  • Professional Challenges in Rehabilitation Practice (15 Points)
  •  Lack of Resources: Shortage of funds, infrastructure, and assistive devices limits effective service
  • delivery.
  •  Shortage of Trained Professionals: Insufficient number of qualified therapists, social workers, and
  • specialists.
  •  Interdisciplinary Coordination Issues: Poor teamwork among doctors, therapists, and social
  • workers affects outcomes.
  •  High Caseload: Professionals often handle many clients, reducing quality of care and individual
  • attention.
  •  Limited Awareness: Lack of awareness among clients and families about rehabilitation services.
  •  Social Stigma: Negative societal attitudes hinder acceptance and participation of persons with
  • disabilities.
  •  Policy Implementation Gaps: Weak enforcement of disability laws and schemes reduces
  • effectiveness.
  •  Ethical Dilemmas: Issues like confidentiality, consent, and autonomy create professional
  • challenges.
  •  Cultural Barriers: Differences in beliefs and traditions may affect acceptance of rehabilitation
  • methods.
  •  Accessibility Issues: Lack of barrier-free environments makes service delivery difficult.
  •  Financial Constraints of Clients: Poverty limits access to treatment and long-term rehabilitation.
  •  Motivation Issues: Clients may lack motivation due to chronic conditions or slow progress.
  •  Technological Limitations: Limited access to advanced rehabilitation technology and assistive
  • tools.
  •  Emotional Burnout: Professionals face stress and burnout due to continuous exposure to
  • challenging cases.
  •  Monitoring and Follow-up Problems: Difficulty in ensuring continuity of care and long-term
  • support.

questions.question: Analyse social challenges. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse social challenges. - An] / [CO4
  •  Social Stigma: Negative attitudes and stereotypes lead to exclusion and discrimination.
  •  Discrimination: Unequal treatment in education, employment, and public life.
  •  Lack of Social Acceptance: Society often fails to accept persons with disabilities as equal members.
  •  Isolation: Limited social interaction results in loneliness and marginalization.
  •  Accessibility Issues: Inaccessible public spaces, transport, and services restrict participation.
  •  Educational Barriers: Lack of inclusive education and support systems.
  •  Employment Challenges: Limited job opportunities and workplace discrimination.
  •  Poverty and Economic Dependence: Disability often leads to financial insecurity.
  •  Gender Discrimination: Women with disabilities face double discrimination.
  •  Cultural Beliefs and Myths: Superstitions and misconceptions affect treatment and inclusion.
  •  Lack of Awareness: Society lacks knowledge about disability rights and capabilities.
  •  Communication Barriers: Difficulty in interaction due to language, sensory, or social factors.
  •  Policy Gaps: Weak implementation of disability-related laws and schemes.
  •  Limited Community Participation: Exclusion from social, cultural, and political activities.
  •  Psychological Impact: Social challenges lead to low self-esteem, stress, and reduced quality of life.

questions.question: Evaluate the disability and identity formation. / [CO2] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the disability and identity formation. -[E] / [CO2
  • Disability and Identity Formation (15 Points)
  •  Concept of Identity: Identity refers to how individuals perceive themselves and how they are
  • recognized by society.
  •  Impact of Disability on Self-Concept: Disability can influence self-esteem, confidence, and
  • personal identity.
  •  Social Labeling: Society often labels persons with disabilities, which may lead to stereotyping and
  • stigma.
  •  Stigma and Discrimination: Negative attitudes affect identity development and social
  • participation.
  •  Internalization of Disability: Individuals may internalize society’s views, leading to positive or
  • negative self-identity.
  •  Positive Identity Formation: With support, individuals can develop a strong, empowered identity
  • beyond disability.
  •  Role of Family: Family acceptance and encouragement help build confidence and self-worth.
  •  Peer Influence: Inclusion in peer groups promotes social identity and belongingness.
  •  Cultural Context: Cultural beliefs and values shape how disability is perceived and experienced.
  •  Education and Awareness: Inclusive education helps in building confidence and reducing identity
  • conflicts.
  •  Role of Rehabilitation Services: Rehabilitation supports independence and enhances self-identity.
  •  Advocacy and Rights Movements: Disability rights movements promote dignity and self-
  • advocacy.
  •  Intersectionality: Identity is shaped by multiple factors like gender, class, and disability together.
  •  Barriers to Identity Development: Lack of opportunities, accessibility issues, and exclusion hinder
  • identity formation.
  •  Empowerment and Inclusion: Social inclusion and equal opportunities strengthen positive identity
  • formation.
